abstract: The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) allows covered imports to be assessed using verified actual emissions or regulatory defaults. This paper examines how the choice of emissions basis influences exporters’ verification, abatement and production decisions under strategic competition. We develop a two-stage Cournot model in which heterogeneous exporters decide whether to verify their emissions and to undertake abatement before competing on quantities. The model incorporates verification costs, free-allocation adjustments, non-negative certificate liability and the incidence of CBAM costs. The analysis shows that higher default values can strengthen verification incentives, while declining free allocation can reduce abatement among verified exporters under certain conditions. Consequently, tighter CBAM treatment may increase emissions associated with modelled EU-bound output, although this outcome depends on abatement-cost structure and becomes more restrictive as output-scaled costs become more important. A steel application combines regulatory parameters with a deterministic sensitivity analysis to identify the regions of parameter space associated with different equilibrium outcomes. The results also show that equilibrium multiplicity and mixed strategies can affect emissions and welfare comparisons. Overall, the findings highlight how default values, verification costs, cost incidence and abatement technology interact to shape exporters’ responses to CBAM.
title: Default emissions values, verification costs and strategic abatement under the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism

abstract: This paper examines whether cultural origin can sustain price premiums independently of institutional certification in spirits pricing. Using a dataset of 4,048 rums from the RumX platform, we employ a layered hedonic approach introducing intrinsic attributes (age, distillation method, raw materials, ABV, packaging), community ratings, and organoleptic perceptions, before adding origin signals across three geographical scales: cultural style (French, English, Spanish), country, and distillery. Hierarchical fixed effects and Ridge regression isolate direct and interaction effects of each layer. Unsupervised Finite Mixture Model clustering validates the cultural taxonomy, recovering latent segments consistent with cultural categories. Results show that cultural style generates significant specific price premiums, outweighing sub-national geographical layers, particularly for French and English styles. Cultural style, derived from the country’s official language, is quasi-exogenous, and its premium survives attribute controls, confirming genuine consumer valuation of symbolic origin rather than correlated production choices. These findings indicate that origin-based price premiums do not rest exclusively on formal certification: cultural style, a broad, legible provenance signal, sustains premiums even where formal certification is limited or absent. Expanding formal geographical-indication schemes may therefore carry risks of rigidity and proliferation without being a prerequisite for origin premiums, a consideration for the design of such schemes.
title: When cultural style outweighs territorial origin: evidence on origin premiums in the rum market

abstract: The development of electromobility has become an integral part of the modern automotive industry worldwide. However, when implementing a new technology, decision-makers face a chicken-and-egg dilemma. It is argued that electric vehicles are needed to drive development or charging infrastructure drives adoption. Answers to these questions vary depending on the parameters chosen. This paper seeks to determine whether they drive each other. It relies on cointegration evidence using data from an emerging, rather than a mature market in electromobility. To empirically verify these relationships, a VECM with bootstrap rank tests and Toda-Yamamoto causality tests in 216 variants were applied. A total of 73 monthly observations from December 2019 to December 2025 were analysed. The main control variable was the price of petrol, while reference rates were included in the robustness analysis. The estimated VECM reveals one long-run relation, conditional on petrol prices, from which charging infrastructure can be excluded. In the short term, charging infrastructure does not Granger-cause BEV adoption, but the test lacks power against published effect sizes. The causality detected from EV adoption to charging infrastructure is not robust. In the main specification, the BEV fleet response to a sustained 1% rise in charging points is 0.53% after two years (95% interval 0.16–1.13). Furthermore, the co-evolution in a four-variable model stems from collinear infrastructure measures and asymptotic tests. For public policy, these results imply that national time series cannot unambiguously tell which should come first and that such series alone justify neither push nor pull policies.
title: Do charging infrastructure and electric vehicle adoption drive each other? The limits of time-series evidence for policy in an emerging electromobility market

abstract: In energy‐only electricity markets, such as the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM), all electricity is bought and sold within the spot market and energy retailers hedge their load using financial contracts. These interrelated markets are key aspects of the NEM design. As governments increasingly decarbonise electricity grids through direct underwriting of variable renewable energy (VRE), they are also replacing the types of contracts available for retail hedging. A recent review of the NEM proposed a series of alternative contracts to both finance new VRE and hedge electricity retailer load. This article models the ability of a suite of different ‘firmed renewables’ derivative contract types to hedge electricity retail load and compares their performance to traditional financial futures and caps contracts currently available to retailers in the NEM under a specific modelled scenario. The results suggest that the contracts proposed by the NEM Review can replicate the proposed benchmark in their ability to hedge retail load.
journal: Australian Journal of Agricultural and Resource Economics
title: Electricity Retailer Hedging Using Fungible Financial Renewable Energy Contracts

abstract: Food markets are becoming increasingly important for rural food security in developing countries, beyond subsistence agriculture. This study examines how rural food markets affect food‐at‐home consumption and nutrient intake among rural residents in three provinces of central China. Greater food market availability increases the consumption of relatively more market‐constrained foods, including meat, aquatic products, eggs and milk and dairy products, while reducing the reliance on relatively less market‐constrained staples, particularly cereals. These changes are associated with improved dietary balance and dietary diversity. Although total energy intake does not change significantly, nutrient composition shifts towards higher animal‐source energy, animal‐source protein and fat intake and lower plant‐source energy, plant‐source protein and carbohydrate intake. The effects also vary across market formats. These findings extend the existing evidence on how rural food markets shape diets and nutrition in developing countries and provide policy implications for improving the availability of nutritious foods in rural areas.

abstract: Using the 2022 wave of the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) and a fuzzy regression-discontinuity (RDD) design at the statutory retirement age, this article estimates the local causal effect of retirement on household consumption and portfolio allocation. We find that retirement triggers a significant reallocation of household budgets. On the consumption side, total expenditure declines by 2.9%. This aggregate decrease is driven by a 4.0% reduction in work-related expenditure and a 2.6% fall in other nondurable expenditures, alongside a more modest 1.4% decrease in food and clothing expenditure. Conversely, recreation and leisure expenditures rise substantially by 3.2%. On the asset side, households shift towards safer and more liquid holdings – demand and term deposits increase by about 11.2% and 6.4%, respectively – accompanied by a significant expansion in housing wealth. Mechanism analysis reveals that changes in time use and heightened precautionary motives underpin these behavioural shifts. The results, robust to a range of checks, are local to compliers induced by the age-60 eligibility rule and inform the design of pension systems and the ‘silver economy’ in ageing societies.

abstract: Coconut plantations support the livelihoods of millions of smallholder families globally, including a high proportion who live in poverty. Many growing regions are caught in a ‘senility trap’, with large areas over the age of 60, with nut yields well-below their potential. Presently, senile palm removal incurs high direct costs and opportunity costs associated with foregone nut production before replanted coconuts become commercially productive. However, demand for coconut engineered wood products (EWPs) could catalyse a circular economy model for the coconut industry. The aim of this study was to determine the farm-scale financial performance and regional-scale economic performance of EWP-assisted coconut plantation rejuvenation. An ex-ante case study analysis was performed for Fiji, a nation with a high proportion of senile coconut plantations on a substantial fraction of the nation’s agricultural land, which is mostly managed by smallholders who experience a high rate of poverty. Financial performance was evaluated based on net annual cash flow and net present value (NPV; r = 10%), while economic performance was evaluated for three regional coconut rejuvenation scenarios and based on gross value of production (GVP), rural employment generation and income-based pro-poor economic growth metrics. The analysis revealed that the addition of an income stream with senile palm removal in the year a site is replanted with coconut seedlings would increase the NPV of farmers by FJ$970/ha relative to retaining the senile coconut plantation. Regional scale adoption could potentially increase GVP from EWP and coconut oil production by tens of millions of Fijian dollars annually, generate hundreds of rural jobs and facilitate relative to strong absolute pro-poor economic growth. These positive findings indicate EWP-assisted coconut plantation rejuvenation has the potential to make substantial contributions to Fiji’s national development goals, including reducing poverty, unemployment and rural-urban migration through decentralised and diversified growth. However, targeted policy reforms are likely to be necessary for this transformative potential to be realised, including property rights to natural resources. Methods and findings are broadly applicable to other coconut growing regions in Asia and the Pacific with high levels of coconut senility.
title: Financial and economic performance of coconut plantation rejuvenation assisted by engineered wood products: A Fijian case study

abstract: We estimate the causal effects of union membership on labour market outcomes for natives and immigrants, exploiting quasi-experimental variation from large increases in Norway’s tax deduction for union dues. Union membership raises earnings and improves employment protection for native workers, while the private returns for non-Western immigrants are substantially smaller and often close to zero. Complementary survey evidence suggests that this gap is not explained by differences in information, preferences, or engagement with unions: immigrants receive similar information when joining, report similar preferences over job amenities, and are more likely than natives to seek union assistance. Instead, the combined administrative and survey evidence is consistent with differences in union-side behaviour. Immigrants report lower satisfaction after contacting unions for support and are more likely to believe that native workers and those with strong local networks receive greater benefits from membership. The impact is most pronounced in concentrated labour markets, indicating that relying on unions to address monopsony-based market failures may unintentionally amplify group inequalities.
title: Union Membership and Native-Immigrant Labour Market Gaps

abstract: We study the mating patterns of non-heterosexual individuals, who represent a significant and increasing portion of the population, particularly among the youth. We estimate a multidimensional matching model of the marriage market where partner’s gender is endogenously chosen conditional on the agent’s sexual orientation, and is subject to trade-offs that depend on both the agents’ preferences and the pool of potential partners. We show that same-sex couples experience lower gains from live-in relationships, a “same-sex penalty”. Absent this penalty, the share of same-sex couples in the U.S. would increase by about 50% (from 1.36% to 2.04% of all couples).
journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
title: Matching on Gender and Sexual Orientation,
title_zh: 按性别与性取向匹配

abstract: This paper provides an empirical, operations-based assessment of routing surplus solar electricity to Bitcoin mining in Korea. We assume a public operator setting with a zero energy cost and over/under-clock scheduling within solar hours. By using the latest mining machine, BITMAIN Antminer S21 XP Hyd Bitcoin Miner, and modeling Bitcoin price with both Random Forest Regressor and Long Short-Term Memory networks, the study quantifies profitability under operational scenarios of 111,269 and 166,887 units. The findings demonstrate that surplus electricity can be transformed into a source of economic value with reducing energy loss, alleviating unresolved payments, and directly contributing to the debt reduction and financial stability of Korea Electric Power Corporation. To our knowledge, this is the first scenario-based empirical evaluation of surplus solar electricity for mining in Korea, linking surplus energy, losses, and operating expenditure. This study not only demonstrates the technical and financial feasibility of such a system but also sets a precedent for future energy policy and Bitcoin infrastructure. It introduces a new way where surplus energy becomes a valuable asset, an innovation that could redefine how nations view grid management, decentralized technologies, and energy economics.
title: Leveraging surplus electricity: Profitability of Bitcoin mining as a national strategy in South Korea

abstract: Technological innovation is an important pillar of energy security (ES). However, systematic evidence remains limited on how different technological pathways are associated with multidimensional ES. Using data from 51 countries over the period 2000-2023, this study applies the global entropy weighting method to construct a four-dimensional ES covering supply, economic, environmental, and social security. It further develops indicators for nine energy technology fields and employs the XGBoost–SHAP approach to examine their relative contributions, directions of association, stage-dependent changes, and interaction structures. The results show that, first, ES generally improves across countries, although no synchronous convergence emerges. Second, Fossil fuel technologies (FF), Renewable energy technologies (RES), and Heat and power generation, storage, and supply technologies (HPGSS) make the largest predictive contributions, while the direction of their SHAP contributions changes across different stages. Third, the technology interaction network centres on FF, with particularly strong interactions involving Nuclear fission and fusion technologies (NFF) and Critical minerals (CM). Fourth, technology priorities vary markedly across security dimensions. Supply security is characterised by broad multi-technology support centred on FF; economic security is primarily associated with FF, Hydrogen, hydrogen-based fuels, and fuel cell technologies (HHBFC), and HPGSS; environmental security is more strongly associated with NFF, HHBFC, and CM; and EEU has the largest predictive contribution to social-security predictions. These findings suggest that energy innovation policy should move beyond simply expanding the overall scale of innovation and instead optimise technology portfolios according to ES vulnerabilities, stages of technological development, and supporting conditions.
title: The energy security paradox of technology innovation in the energy transition

abstract: Though active institutional investors play a predominant role in stock price discovery, little is known about the real effects of the attention they pay to individual stocks. We find that exogenous reductions in the attention paid by dedicated institutions cause decreases in information production, which, in turn, worsens the stock's liquidity and informational price efficiency, ultimately resulting in a higher cost of capital and less real investment. Exogenous reductions in attention paid by transient institutions reduce informed trading and improve equity market quality. We infer that active institutional investor attention has important real causal effects that vary by institution type.
title: Dedicated vs Transient: Not all institutional attention is good attention

abstract: Motivated by the high prices of branded/patented pharmaceuticals in many parts of the world, this paper analyzes price regulations in a two-country (home and foreign) model where a single home firm serves both markets and its R&D investment determines product quality. We study two types of price regulations: direct price controls (PCs) and external reference pricing (ERP) under which the price that the firm is permitted to charge locally depends upon its price abroad. We show that although ERP undermines R&D incentives, its implementation can raise home welfare. However, home’s optimal ERP policy is too restrictive from a joint welfare perspective. Furthermore, if the foreign market is subject to a PC, home prefers ERP to a PC due to strategic considerations that come into play due to the international price linkage created by ERP.
title: External reference pricing versus price controls under endogenous product quality
title_zh: 外部参考定价与价格管制：内生产品质量下的比较

abstract: A seller wants to sell an item to n buyers. Buyer valuations are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) according to a distribution unknown to the seller; the seller only knows that the support is included in [a, b]. To be robust, the seller chooses a dominant strategy incentive compatible mechanism that optimizes the worst-case performance relative to the ideal expected revenue the seller could have collected with knowledge of buyers’ valuations. Our analysis unifies the regret and the ratio objectives. For these objectives, we derive an optimal mechanism and the corresponding performance in quasi-closed form, as a function of the support information [a, b] and the number of buyers n. Our analysis reveals three regimes of support information and a new class of robust mechanisms. (i) When a/b is below a threshold, the optimal mechanism is a second-price auction (SPA) with random reserve, a focal class in earlier literature. (ii) When a/b is above another threshold, SPAs are strictly suboptimal, and an optimal mechanism belongs to a class of mechanisms we introduce, which we call pooling auctions (POOL); whenever the highest value is above a threshold, the mechanism still allocates to the highest bidder, but otherwise the mechanism allocates to a uniformly random buyer, that is, pools low types. (iii) When a/b is between two thresholds, a randomization between SPA and POOL is optimal. We also characterize optimal mechanisms within nested central subclasses of mechanisms: standard mechanisms that only allocate to the highest bidder, SPA with random reserve, and SPA with no reserve. We show strict separations in terms of performance across classes, implying that deviating from standard mechanisms is necessary for robustness. Lastly, we show that the same results hold under other distribution classes that capture “positive dependence,” namely i.i.d., mixture of i.i.d., and exchangeable and affiliated distributions, as well as i.i.d. regular distributions. This paper was accepted by David Simchi-Levi, revenue management and market analytics. Supplemental Material: The online appendices are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.02703 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)

abstract: We propose a simple framework for estimating the pricing kernel in factor space by constructing the mean–variance efficient factor portfolio via an ordinary least squares formulation with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regularization. The method accommodates high-dimensional settings in which the number of candidate factors exceeds the sample size and automatically shrinks redundant factor weights toward zero. We show theoretically that the out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of the estimated portfolio converges to the theoretical maximum at the fastest rate among existing regression-based approaches. Applying the method to 174 characteristic-based factors together with the market factor, we obtain an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 3.59, substantially outperforming competing strategies and delivering the smallest aggregate pricing errors. The selected factors vary over time in both composition and number, averaging about 50. We further develop a model comparison test and reject the hypothesis that eight widely used sparse factor models are sufficient to span the pricing kernel. This paper was accepted by Kay Giesecke, finance. Funding: This work was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72671091, 72371079, and 72501192, and Key Program 72432005] and the Science and Technology Planning Project of Guangdong Province [Grant 2023B1515020045]. abstract: This study investigates the unintended effect of the introduction of the 2011 Social Insurance Law on corporate pollution emissions. Using a difference-in-differences framework, our analysis reveals that enhanced social insurance contributions lead to higher industrial pollution emissions, as measured by chemical oxygen demand and wastewater emissions. The mechanism analysis indicates that the enforcement of the law increases firms’ labor costs and financial distress, motivating them to reduce efforts on end-of-pipe treatment activities and measures taken during the production process, which results in higher pollution emission intensity. Our study highlights the potential conflict between employee protection and corporate environmental goals. Further analysis suggests that stronger environmental monitoring and environmental, social, and governance disclosure requirements can partially mitigate this tradeoff, providing valuable insights for policymakers. This paper was accepted by Caroline Flammer, sustainability. Funding: Y. Li acknowledges research support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72403026]. Y. Qin acknowledges research support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72342031]. abstract: We show that a firm’s expertise in managing specific inputs—its core competence—is a key driver of diversifying mergers. While prior work shows that such capabilities drive organic, within-firm product expansion, we demonstrate that they also motivate firms’ inorganic growth through acquisition of external firms. Using China’s 2001 WTO accession as a natural experiment, we find that a reduction in tariffs on common inputs of two industries significantly increases the likelihood of a diversifying merger between these two industries. The effect is concentrated in differentiated and innovation-intensive inputs, indicating that the valuable capability lies in mastering complex, knowledge-intensive inputs rather than in sourcing generic ones. The main result holds in a global sample covering 71 economies. Our findings extend the core competence theory by highlighting how input-related capabilities shape firm boundaries across industries.

abstract: Digital platforms collect extensive personal information from users while often also providing credit services. We study the interaction between data use and credit provision. Data use creates incentives for a monopolistic platform to subsidize credit, enabling it to compete with traditional financial institutions even when it faces higher costs. Credit services allow the platform to manipulate buyers’ outside options, extract greater surplus, and raise the value of using data. This may lead to socially inefficient outcomes. When platform competition is considered, platforms may specialize, with some focusing on data use and others on privacy. When credit provision is possible, the set of parameters under which platforms use buyers’ data expands. Finally, under certain conditions, a platform monetizes its data by selling it to a platform that specializes solely in credit services.
title: Credit, Privacy, and Data Monetization by Digital Platforms

abstract: Official inflation statistics in transitional economies often suffer from measurement biases. This paper extends the Nakamura-Steinsson-Liu Pooled Engel Curve Methodology to estimate bias-adjusted annual inflation rates in China up to 2024. To overcome the 2013–2015 household survey reform, we derive the subcategory equation’s dependent variable as the logarithm of quantity, splicing estimates into one bias-adjusted inflation series (1996–2024). The results reveal China is still smoothing its CPI inflation reality. Furthermore, we find the inflation dynamics pattern has shifted away from the hog cycle since the COVID-19 pandemic.

abstract: Voluntary peatland rewetting can contribute to climate change mitigation, but farmer participation remains limited. Drawing on a purposively recruited sample of 141 German farmers surveyed in 2025 (90 managing peatland), this study examines preferences for a compensation scheme and factors associated with outright rejection of participation. Farmers clearly prefer to have authority over the amount of rewetting. In paired comparisons of a scheme's components, analyzed with Bradley–Terry models, respondents placed the greatest relative weight on autonomy over the degree of rewetting. This was followed by future land-use options and then compensation for land value losses. A speed bonus for early application received the lowest relative priority in the paired comparisons. Respondents with and without peatland showed the same estimated ranking of scheme components, with no statistically significant differences in preference strengths, while the two groups differ markedly in farm structure, soil quality, and altruistic orientation, suggesting that scheme architecture may be broadly transferable while targeting and outreach require tailoring. Among peatland farmers, 42% showed some interest or engagement while 24% reported outright rejection. Such rejection is associated with lower altruism and weaker climate-change attitudes according to bias-reduced Firth logistic regression. Among peatland respondents considering rewetting but not yet implementing it (Rogers stages 2–4; n = 29), descriptive COM-B results indicated stronger reported needs related to capability and opportunity than to motivation. Specifically, the capability needs analysis points to a lack of resources such as credible information on the economic viability of rewetted land and the opportunity needs analysis points to a lack of services such as advisory support and peer exchange. Reported barriers centered on long-term economic uncertainty and limited trust in funding schemes. Overall, these exploratory findings suggest that respondents prioritize autonomy, future flexibility, and long-term institutional credibility over short-term financial incentives alone. The results provide exploratory, policy-relevant insights for peatland rewetting program design in Germany and, potentially, in comparable contexts.
title: German farmers' preferences for peatland rewetting schemes: Autonomy, flexibility and institutional trust

abstract: We study how redistribution between asset holders and non‐asset holders links macroeconomic fluctuations to expected stock returns. Aggregate and relative consumption growth forecast excess returns with opposite signs and at different horizons. We interpret these patterns using a production‐based asset‐pricing model with limited participation and external habits. Aggregate (relative) consumption captures variation in the price (quantity) of risk. Technology shocks drive macroeconomic fluctuations, whereas redistributive shocks generate large short‐run movements in inequality and are the main source of priced risk. This points to a macro‐finance disconnect between the drivers of business cycles and those governing risk premia.
title: Asset Market Participation, Redistribution, and Asset Pricing

abstract: We propose a nonrecursive VAR identification strategy that separately identifies short‐term and long‐term uncertainty shocks by exploiting sign restrictions implied by a stylized framework and a DSGE model featuring both types of shocks. We find that long‐term uncertainty shocks exert strong and persistent effects on real activity, whereas short‐term shocks have limited real effects. We use the DSGE model to study their differential propagation and show that time‐to‐build is an important ingredient allowing the model to account for the stark empirical asymmetry in investment and, in turn, output—both contract sharply after long‐term shocks but only modestly after short‐term shocks.
title: Real Activity and Uncertainty Shocks: The Long and the Short of It

abstract: I propose a mechanism through which institutional investors’ correlated demand shocks provide a source of market risk in asset pricing. Institutional investors have mandates to beat a similar market index. During periods of strong stock market performance, their incentive to outperform intensifies as more of them fall short of the market index. This incentive induces procyclical risk-taking behavior, generating correlated demand that elevates the market betas and risk premia of exposed stocks. Quasi-experiments using exogenous changes in index membership support a causal interpretation of the mechanism. Elevated betas are associated with a higher perceived cost of capital and reduced firm investment. (JEL G1, G2)
title: Correlated Demand Shocks and Asset Pricing
title_zh: 相关需求冲击与资产定价

abstract: While governments worldwide heavily invest in technology finance (TF) to catalyze emerging industries, the relative efficacy of public versus market mechanisms remains a critical puzzle. Using prefecture-level panel data from China for 2010–2021, this paper employs two-way fixed effects and panel threshold models to examine the relationships of public technology finance (PTF) and market technology finance (MTF) with the development of emerging industries (DEI). The results show that PTF has no significant standalone association with DEI, but its relationship with DEI is stronger at higher levels of MTF. The positive MTF–DEI relationship is concentrated in technology loans from financial institutions. Innovation quality is a potential channel in the MTF–DEI relationship, which is stronger above the estimated quality threshold. Higher government support is associated with a stronger MTF–DEI relationship, while the positive PTF–MTF interaction is weaker above the estimated support threshold. Both PTF and MTF have stronger positive relationships with DEI in cities with more developed digital economies. These findings provide new evidence for designing technology finance policies that combine market allocation with targeted public support.

abstract: This study examines the impact of ‘Specialized, Sophisticated, Unique and New’ Little Giant Enterprises government direct subsidy policy on firms’ innovation quantity and quality in China. Based on the data of 22,330 Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2024, this paper reveals that although this government subsidy policy generates positive effects on the quantity of firms’ innovation, it exerts negative influences on the innovation quality simultaneously and only boosts the innovation quantity in developed regions. Mechanism analysis reveals that the implementation of government direct subsidy policy decreases innovation quality through cutting R&D expenditure per R&D staff, while it also boosts innovation quantity through raising R&D investment intensity. This study further explores the spatial spillover effects of this subsidy policy by using spatial causal inference. The results indicate that this subsidy policy also generates significant positive spillover effects on innovation quantity and negative spillover effects on innovation quality.

abstract: We examine whether investors value the separation of disclosure duties from managerial roles within top management. We use China’s Board Secretary Regulation, which restricts listed firms’ board secretaries from concurrently holding certain senior managerial positions. Using an event-study design around the consultation draft and final-rule announcements, we find that firms whose board secretaries held restricted concurrent appointments experienced significantly higher cumulative abnormal returns than firms without such appointments. The results are robust to alternative expected-return models, event windows and propensity-score matching. The return differential increases with prior reporting-related inquiry letters and the number of restricted concurrent positions, consistent with investors anticipating benefits from greater disclosure independence and fewer competing demands on attention. For CFO–board secretary duality, the reaction is positive and significant under weak governance but insignificant under strong governance, suggesting that investors weigh the information benefits of this combination against its governance costs. Stronger reactions also occur among firms with male board secretaries, lower analyst coverage and lower regional marketization. Overall, the findings suggest that investors expected mandated role separation to improve disclosure governance, particularly where disclosure-governance concerns are greater and external monitoring is weaker.

abstract: When a counter-proposal is made to an initiative to change the Swiss constitution, the citizenry makes three binary majority choices: the initiative versus the status quo, the counter-proposal versus the status quo, and the initiative versus the counter-proposal as a tie-breaker. If the three majority choices form a cycle, the current rule selects the alternative that beats the status quo. This rule may lead to strategic voting. We suggest breaking cycles differently by choosing the middle alternative in case of a cycle, which will normally be the counter-proposal. More precisely, we study Condorcet-consistent pairwise majority voting procedures when preferences are single-peaked and their distribution is common knowledge. We then show that whenever a strong Nash equilibrium exists, its outcome is the same as under sincere voting, and we characterize the cycle-breaking defaults for which sincere voting is itself a strong Nash equilibrium. In particular, among procedures that use the same default for both possible cycles, the middle alternative is the unique common default.
title: A Better Cycle-Breaker for Direct Democracy?
title_zh: 更优的直接民主周期打破机制？

abstract: Decarbonising the hard-to-abate maritime and aviation transport sectors will be challenging. Alternative renewable fuels, such as biofuels and E-fuels, show promising potential for substituting traditional fossil fuels, but carry challenges regarding the expansion of variable renewable energy (VRE) and the availability of sustainable biomass. This study assesses these challenges and regional impacts using a comprehensive sector-coupled energy system modelling framework applied to Europe. Under high biomass availability, a documented substitution effect allows the share of E-kerosene and biokerosene to shift with VRE accessibility, whereas this flexibility declines under biomass scarcity. These differences are reflected in fuel costs: aviation fuel prices are more sensitive to biomass scarcity, while maritime fuel prices are more sensitive to VRE restrictions. Regional resource availability reshapes renewable fuel production and trade. Under the modelling assumptions, accessible VRE resources favour E-fuel supply-chains from Spain, while lower VRE accessibility increases the role of biomass-rich countries, including Germany and Poland, as exporters. Constrained VRE deployment results in increased infrastructure needs, lowers average renewable capacity factors, and raises total system costs by up to 9%. Finally, increasing scarcity increases the importance of carbon management. Biomass is prioritised for fuel production and industrial applications coupled with carbon capture, while direct air capture and carbon reuse become increasingly important for meeting fuel demand. These results highlight the need for coordinated policies on biomass utilisation, VRE deployment, carbon management, and infrastructure planning to achieve cost-efficient decarbonisation of Europe's hard-to-abate transport sectors.
abstract_zh: 难以减排的海运和航空运输部门脱碳将颇具挑战性。生物燃料和电制燃料等替代可再生燃料展现出替代传统化石燃料的潜力，但在可变可再生能源（VRE）扩张和可持续生物质可用性方面面临挑战。本研究采用一个综合的部门耦合能源系统建模框架应用于欧洲，评估这些挑战及区域影响。在生物质高可用性下，一种有文献记载的替代效应使得电制煤油和生物煤油的比例可随VRE可及性变化而转移，而在生物质稀缺下这种灵活性下降。这些差异反映在燃料成本上：航空燃料价格对生物质稀缺更为敏感，而海运燃料价格对VRE限制更为敏感。区域资源可用性重塑可再生燃料生产和贸易。在建模假设下，可及的VRE资源有利于来自西班牙的电制燃料供应链，而较低的VRE可及性则增强了包括德国和波兰在内的生物质丰富国家作为出口国的作用。受限的VRE部署导致基础设施需求增加，降低平均可再生容量系数，并使系统总成本增加高达9%。最后，日益加剧的稀缺性提高了碳管理的重要性。生物质被优先用于燃料生产及与碳捕集相结合的工业应用，而直接空气捕集和碳再利用对于满足燃料需求变得日益重要。这些结果凸显了在生物质利用、VRE部署、碳管理和基础设施规划方面采取协调政策的必要性，以实现欧洲难以减排运输部门的经济高效脱碳。
title: Renewable fuels for hard-to-abate transportation: Exploring the impact of biomass availability and variable renewable potentials

abstract: This study investigates how energy uncertainty relates to corporate innovation in China, where rising energy volatility and sustainability concerns have intensified firms’ strategic responses to external uncertainty. Using panel regression analyses, we find that high energy uncertainty is positively associated with firms’ R&D activities, suggesting that firms respond proactively to energy-related risks by increasing innovation efforts rather than reducing them. We further identify the cost of goods sold as a potential channel, indicating that rising input costs may incentivize firms to pursue innovation to improve operational efficiency and productivity. This positive relationship is significantly stronger among state-owned enterprises and firms located in low-carbon pilot cities, highlighting the important moderating role of institutional support and environmental policy. Extending the analysis to patenting activity, we find consistent evidence that energy uncertainty increases both green and non-green patent outputs. Overall, our findings have policy implications for the role of institutional support and sustainability-oriented policies in promoting innovation in uncertain energy conditions.

abstract: Population ageing has intensified the need for robust measures of wellbeing beyond income and morbidity. This study examines wellbeing from the joint determination of perceived health, life satisfaction and quality of life among older adults. Using data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) covering seven European countries, we estimate recursive semi-ordered probit models with full-information maximum likelihood. Our empirical strategy allows for correlated unobservables and employs household financial stress and household size as instruments to correct for endogeneity. The results demonstrate that perceived health is a central endogenous driver of both life satisfaction and quality of life, with effects strongest among individuals at lower levels of wellbeing. Reciprocal feedback from subjective wellbeing to health perceptions is also statistically significant, confirming simultaneity across outcomes. While the existence of these relationships is consistent across countries, their magnitude varies systematically across welfare regimes, reflecting differences in institutional support and economic vulnerability. From a policy perspective, the findings suggest that subjective wellbeing is multidimensional and that healthy ageing with positive functioning results from an integrated health and social policies. Methodologically, this study contributes to a parsimonious econometric framework for analysing multidimensional wellbeing in different policy settings.
title: Health, Life Satisfaction, and Quality of Life in Ageing Economies: Modelling for Unfolding Endogeneity

abstract: Did immigration from Eastern Europe increase Euroscepticism in Britain? This study examines how this migration wave influenced British Euroscepticism. Using longitudinal survey data and an instrumental variable strategy, I provide causal evidence that the inflow of Eastern European migrants led to increased Eurosceptic attitudes. The migration inflow also increased comparative national attachment and perceived crime risk.

abstract: The 20th century shift from sterling to the dollar is often cited as evidence that currency dominance is not forever. This column presents a nonlinear model of the international monetary system calibrated on historical events. Shifts in dominance require large, simultaneous combinations of shocks, with democracy and conflicts playing a central role. Stress tests suggest that dollar dominance is resilient: a decline would require repeated shocks in the US alongside major reforms in China and Europe. Parallels between the dollar’s rise in the 20th century and that of the renminbi in the 21st century should be treated with extreme caution.
abstract_zh: 20世纪从英镑到美元的转变常被引为货币主导地位并非永恒的证据。本专栏提出一个基于历史事件校准的国际货币体系非线性模型。主导地位的转变需要大规模、同时发生的冲击组合，其中民主与冲突发挥核心作用。压力测试表明，美元主导地位具有韧性：其衰落需要美国反复遭受冲击，同时中国和欧洲进行重大改革。应将20世纪美元崛起与21世纪人民币崛起之间的类比极为谨慎地对待。

abstract: International financial integration is often measured through national totals. Yet these totals can conceal very different experiences across firms. Using comprehensive French microdata, this column shows that most financially internationalised firms raise foreign equity without investing abroad, while a small group of large firms dominates cross-border positions. Foreign funding is associated with greater equity financing, lower bank debt, and higher investment. This heterogeneity also means that aggregate estimates understate the importance of country factors for the cross-border allocations of the typical firm.
abstract_zh: 国际金融一体化通常通过国家总量来衡量。然而，这些总量可能掩盖了企业间截然不同的经历。利用全面的法国微观数据，本专栏表明，大多数金融国际化企业筹集外国股权但并未对外投资，而一小部分大型企业主导了跨境头寸。外国融资与更高的股权融资、更低的银行债务和更高的投资相关联。这种异质性也意味着，总量估计低估了国家因素对典型企业跨境配置的重要性。

abstract: This paper develops a two-dimensional crisis typology that classifies the impact of major crisis episodes on return spillover connectedness across energy transition metals (ETM) markets. Using daily data for 17 metals, spanning base metals, precious metals, battery metals, and technology metals, and the rolling-window Diebold–Yılmaz (2012) connectedness framework, the paper classifies 11 crisis events between 2017 and 2025 along two orthogonal axes: the direction of the connectedness shift (integration vs. fragmentation) and the stability of the response (volatile vs. stable), with the latter benchmarked against a bootstrap-derived threshold from pre-crisis markets. The typology reveals a fragmentation paradox: supply-side shocks (armed conflicts and bilateral trade restrictions) consistently decrease market connectedness, while demand-side shocks (pandemics, monetary tightening, and financial crises) consistently increase it. This dichotomy, which is robustly preserved across all 25 event-study window specifications, challenges the prevailing assumption in the connectedness literature that crises uniformly amplify systemic risk through heightened spillovers. The mechanism is grounded in the distinction between common-factor and idiosyncratic transmission channels: supply disruptions affect individual metals asymmetrically based on their geographic exposure, fragmenting the co-movement structure, while demand shocks operate through common macroeconomic channels that drive all metals together. The typology has implications for strategic reserves policy, portfolio hedging, and energy transition risk assessment, suggesting that geopolitical risk to critical minerals supply chains is more modular than the contagion hypothesis predicts.
abstract_zh: 本文构建了一个二维危机类型学，用于分类重大危机事件对能源转型金属（ETM）市场间收益溢出关联性的影响。基于17种金属（涵盖基本金属、贵金属、电池金属和技术金属）的日度数据，并采用滚动窗口Diebold–Yılmaz（2012）关联性框架，本文将2017年至2025年间的11次危机事件沿两条正交轴进行分类：关联性变化的方向（整合与碎片化）和响应的稳定性（波动与稳定），后者以危机前市场通过自助法得出的阈值为基准。该类型学揭示了一个碎片化悖论：供给侧冲击（武装冲突和双边贸易限制）持续降低市场关联性，而需求侧冲击（流行病、货币紧缩和金融危机）持续提高市场关联性。这一二分法在所有25种事件研究窗口设定下均稳健保持，挑战了关联性文献中关于危机通过加剧溢出效应统一放大系统性风险的主流假设。其机制根植于共同因子与特质性传导渠道的区分：供给中断基于各金属的地理暴露对其产生不对称影响，从而碎片化共同运动结构；而需求冲击通过驱动所有金属共同运动的共同宏观经济渠道发挥作用。该类型学对战略储备政策、投资组合对冲和能源转型风险评估具有启示意义，表明关键矿产供应链的地缘政治风险比传染假说所预测的更具模块化特征。
title: Do crises integrate or fragment energy transition metals markets? Evidence from a connectedness-based crisis typology
title_zh: 危机是整合还是分裂能源转型金属市场？——基于连通性危机类型学的证据

abstract: I study spillovers from U.S. bond supply shocks, identified from yield moves around U.S. Treasury auction announcements. Using the shocks as instruments in daily and monthly local projections for AEs and EMs, I find substantial pass-through to global long-term rates. A debt expansion shock that raises the U.S. 10-year yield by 10 bps lifts foreign 10-year yields by roughly 7 bps within a few business days. Monthly aggregation shows contractionary real effects: U.S. industrial production falls up to 0.4 percent after eight months and foreign industrial production by a comparable amount, around 0.4 percent, with a more persistent profile. The foreign contraction reflects financial tightening, exchange-rate depreciation, and weaker U.S. demand. Spillovers are heterogeneous: moving from the 25th to 75th percentile of foreign investor participation deepens the IP decline by 0.5 pp. Results are robust to a demand-side shock and consistent with the relevant benchmarks, highlighting U.S. bond supply as a key driver of global financial conditions and real activity, amplified by foreign investor participation and weak domestic fundamentals.

abstract: This paper estimates the macroeconomic effects of forced displacement on host economies in SubSaharan Africa, drawing on cross-country panel data and country case studies of Burkina Faso, South Sudan, and Uganda to provide granular evidence on the consequences of spatial concentrations of forcibly displaced persons within countries. Estimates from a difference-in-differences local projections (LP-DiD) framework do not suggest that large refugee inflows significantly affect host-country GDP, inflation, or the current account balance over a five-year horizon. The effects on the primary fiscal balance also appear to be muted, yet this masks offsetting fiscal dynamics: government expenditures rise and fiscal revenues increase (mainly through taxes). These results are robust to restricting the control group to Sub-Saharan African economies. Under a broader treatment definition that captures the total displaced population (refugees and internally displaced persons), the GDP response turns significantly negative and intensifies with displacement severity, though this estimate is best interpreted as an upper bound because it cannot be fully separated from the effects of conflict itself that generates displacement. The cross-country findings are consistent with the case studies, which indicate generally muted effects on aggregate food inflation and wages. Beneath this muted aggregate response, however, a consistent pattern emerges across cases: prices of imported and processed staples rise, while those of locally produced cereals stay flat or fall. The case studies also yield mixed evidence regarding the impacts of displacement inflows on consumption and labor force participation, with such inflows reducing host employment in Burkina Faso but raising it in Uganda.
authors: Hany Abdel-Latif & Mr. Antonio David & Mouhamadou Moustapha Ly & Elisee Wendlassida Miningou & Masateru Okamoto & Alex Vaval Pierre-Charles
title: Macroeconomic Effects of Forced Displacement in Sub-Saharan Africa

abstract: The literature characterizes zombie firms as economically unviable companies that continue to operate. This paper proposes that the majority of zombie firms can be viable, with positive continuation value, and arise endogenously from productivity shocks. Drawing on firm-level data covering the universe of Canadian firms and seven European countries, we document five stylized facts: zombie firms are widespread, unprofitable, unproductive, micro-sized, and transitory. We rationalize these findings by building a general equilibrium model of heterogeneous firms that abstracts from the conventional distortions thought to explain zombie firms. We show that standard productivity shocks are sufficient to explain the empirical patterns, and that the volatility of these shocks can be a key determinant of viable zombie firms, generating shares up to 35%. Since this volatility can also raise aggregate productivity and household utility, the presence of zombie firms is not a sufficient condition for lower welfare. Using a model-based definition to distinguish viability, we find limited evidence—around 0.25%—of unviable zombie firms in the data. Our results challenge the prevailing view that persistently weak firms are unviable and suggest that existing zombie firm measures likely capture viable firms.
authors: Alexander Amundsen & Amélie Lafrance-Cooke & Danny Leung
title: Rethinking Zombie Firms: From Volatility to Viability
title_zh: 重新审视僵尸企业：从波动性到生存能力

abstract: This paper analyzes how achieving Europe’s medium-term greenhouse gas mitigation targets enhances energy security, defined as the cushioning of the adverse macroeconomic impact of oil and gas price shocks. It uses the IMF’s Global Macroeconomic Model of the Energy Transition, which combines a rich set of New-Keynesian features with a detailed representation of fossil fuel use, including granular modelling of the transport and heating sectors. Future oil and gas price shocks are simulated in a scenario where Europe’s mitigation policy agenda has been fully implemented (and mitigation targets are met), and in a hypothetical scenario where mitigation policy has remained constant at the current level of ambition. A comparison shows that the policy agenda substantially dampens future shock transmission. The inflationary impact of both shocks is close to 40 percent larger under constant policies than under the mitigation agenda, and for oil shocks, the output decline is about twice as large. These energy security co-benefits materialize gradually as the economy adjusts to the mitigation agenda, and are shown to depend on ETS2, the new emissions trading system covering transportation and buildings. An additional exercise proxies for merit-order electricity pricing. In these simulations, the mitigation agenda further reduces pass-through from gas price shocks to electricity prices, thereby enhancing the macroeconomic stabilizing effects.
title: The EU’s Energy Transition and Fuel Price Shocks
title_zh: 欧盟能源转型与燃料价格冲击

abstract: How are inflation expectations affected by foreign supply shocks? We show that, beyond bilateral exposure, a second network matters: the one linking forecasters to the countries they cover. Using forecasterlevel expectations around conflict episodes—precisely dated supply shocks that raise inflation through trade and energy linkages—we find that expectations are revised upward gradually in the days following a conflict. Within the same country and day, forecasters who cover the conflict country revise by 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points less than those who do not, and the differential roughly triples where bilateral exposure is highest. We rationalize this in a model where a public narrative overstates spillovers in proportion to bilateral exposure, and only forecasters covering the conflict country can discount it. The consensus therefore inherits a bias largest where exposure is high and coverage thin, and a central bank reading it at face value tightens more than fundamentals warrant.
title: Information Networks and Inflation Expectations: Evidence from Professional Forecasters and Conflicts
title_zh: 信息网络与通胀预期：来自专业预测者与冲突的证据

abstract: Revenue mobilization is a key objective in many IMF-supported programs, yet tax revenue-to-GDP forecasts often fall short of outcomes. This paper analyzes the underlying drivers of these forecast misses by leveraging two novel global datasets on tax policy yields and tax administration capacity. It finds that tax revenue-to-GDP forecast errors are primarily driven by over-optimism in forecasted yields of tax policy measures and tax buoyancy assumptions, as well as macroeconomic forecast errors, particularly for growth and trade openness. Stronger tax administration capacity and well-implemented and high-quality revenue related structural reforms are associated with lower forecast errors. Additional empirical analysis shows that over-optimism in forecasted tax policy yields declines significantly when revenue measures are well-designed, part of large-measure revenue packages, and accompanied by high-quality revenue-related structural reforms. Improving forecast realism requires better-grounded yield estimations and tax buoyancy assumptions, explicit consideration of implementation capacity, and a focus on well-designed revenue-related structural reforms.
authors: Jean-Marc Atsebi & Qiaoe Chen & Nikolay Gueorguiev & Magali Pinat
title: Understanding Over-Optimism in Tax Revenue-to-GDP Forecasts under IMF-supported Programs
title_zh: 理解IMF支持项目下税收占GDP预测的过度乐观

abstract: This paper assesses the effectiveness of Morocco’s monetary policy transmission since 2018 in light of reforms aimed at modernizing the policy framework. Over the past decade, Morocco has introduced greater exchange rate flexibility, strengthened the legal and operational focus on price stability, and enhanced central bank communication—measures intended to anchor inflation expectations and improve transmission. Drawing on several years of post-reform data, we use a two-step empirical strategy: (i) identifying exogenous monetary policy shocks through a Taylor-rule-based approach leveraging Bank Al-Maghrib’s forecasts, and (ii) estimating their dynamic effects via local projections, a flexible approach well suited to settings with structural change and limited data. Our findings indicate that transmission to output and inflation has strengthened post-reform: a 1 percentage point policy rate hike reduces output by about 0.3 percent and inflation by 0.1 percent, compared to 0.1 and 0.05 percent pre-reform, respectively. However, responses remain delayed and muted relative to benchmark estimates for other emerging markets. Analysis of transmission channels shows the interest rate channel is most active, the credit channel is partially effective, and the exchange rate channel is stronger post-reform, while the asset price and expectations channels remain weak. These findings provide important insights for Morocco’s ongoing transition to an inflation targeting regime.
authors: Ms. Nadia Mounir & Hannah C Brown
title: Effectiveness of Monetary Policy Transmission in Morocco amid Reforms to the Monetary Policy Framework
title_zh: 摩洛哥货币政策框架改革中货币政策传导的有效性

abstract: Recurring climate-related natural disasters pose significant macroeconomic and fiscal risks for highly exposed countries. We extend the Debt, Investment, Growth, and Natural Disasters (DIGNAD) model to incorporate Annual Average Loss (AAL) metrics, capturing the cumulative macro-fiscal effects of repeated natural disaster shocks. The augmented DIGNAD framework introduces recurring annual capital losses and negative productivity shocks, yielding more realistic growth and public debt trajectories under persistent disaster risk. We quantify the GDP losses from recurrent natural disasters and examine the trade-offs between higher adaptation investment (leading to higher recovered growth) and public debt accumulation. Using cross-country simulations for 33 disaster-prone economies and case studies (the Philippines, Mauritania, and Barbados), we find substantial heterogeneity in disaster impacts and adaptation effectiveness. Comparing risk-adjusted baseline projections with scenarios of scaled-up resilient vs. standard infrastructure investment, we find that investing in resilient public capital can significantly mitigate output losses in the long-term, albeit at the cost of higher public debt.
authors: Mr. Giovanni Melina & Mr. Mehdi Raissi & Azar Sultanov & Mr. Bruno Versailles
title: Recurring Natural Disasters and Macroeconomic Scarring: A Risk Adjusted DIGNAD Framework
title_zh: 反复自然灾害与宏观经济创伤：一个风险调整的DIGNAD框架

abstract: We introduce the Global Fiscal Actions (GFA) Dataset, the first quarterly global narrative database of discretionary fiscal policy actions, covering 142 countries since 1990. GFA combines Economist Intelligence Unit country reports with large language models to systematically identify and classify tax and spending measures, together with their motivations, timing, implementation status, and supporting evidence. We validate the dataset against economists

title: The Global Fiscal Actions (GFA) Dataset
title_zh: 全球财政行动（GFA）数据集
